prompt.context_jp: その気遣いに、ハナの肩の力___少しだけ抜けていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナの肩の力___少しだけ抜けていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks this subtle bodily change as newly observed?

feedback.correct_en: The relaxing of her shoulders is a new, event-like observation triggered by his thoughtfulness — that calls for が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would reframe '肩の力' as an established topic being characterized, which doesn't fit a sudden change. も implies 'also,' which has no antecedent here.

contrast_examples.en: A wind blew suddenly — が for a fresh event.
The wind has stopped now — は for a topic being updated.

prompt.context_jp: 誰にも見せられぬこの手仕事だけ___、彼女と世界とをつなぐ細い糸だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: この手仕事だけ___、彼女と世界とをつなぐ細い糸だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after だけ to exhaustively identify what connects her to the world?

feedback.correct_en: 'This handwork and only this' is being singled out as the sole thing linking her to the world — classic exhaustive-listing が after だけ.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would soften to 'at least this,' losing the 'this alone is it' identification. に is a wrong grammatical slot here.

contrast_examples.en: He alone knows — exhaustive が.
He alone doesn't know (contrast with others) — different nuance.

prompt.context_jp: 仕上げの一粒を型から外すとき、ハナ___初めて小さな笑みを浮かべた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナ___初めて小さな笑みを浮かべた。
prompt.prompt_en: Hana is already the chapter's focal character. Which particle fits here?

feedback.correct_en: Hana is the ongoing topic of this scene; は continues to anchor her as the one whose action is being described.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as new information, which is odd mid-scene. で marks location/means, not a subject.

contrast_examples.en: Hana (topic, already known) smiled.

contrast_examples.jp: そのとき、ハナが入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: Just then, Hana (new on scene) entered.

prompt.context_jp: 職人の目___一瞬鋭くなり、それから驚きに変わっていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 職人の目___一瞬鋭くなり、それから驚きに変わっていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this momentary, witnessed change?

feedback.correct_en: The sharpening of her eyes is observed as a fresh, event-like reaction — が delivers that live-camera feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 職人の目 into an established topic being generalized about, which clashes with the one-time 一瞬 moment. を is for direct objects.

contrast_examples.en: His eyes flashed — observed event, が.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の目はいつも優しい。
contrast_examples.en: His eyes are always gentle — characterizing topic, は.

prompt.context_jp: 先輩たちに認めてもらえたこと___、彼にとっては何よりの報酬だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 先輩たちに認めてもらえたこと___、彼にとっては何よりの報酬だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle identifies what, above all else, was his reward?

feedback.correct_en: 'Being recognized' is being singled out as the specific thing that is his greatest reward — exhaustive-listing が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would merely topicalize it ('as for being recognized...'), weakening the 'this is THE reward' identification. で has no fitting role.

contrast_examples.jp: この一言が何よりうれしい。
contrast_examples.en: This one word is more welcome than anything — が for identification.
As for this word, it's welcome — plain topic comment.

prompt.context_jp: しかしその温度差___、日に日に埋めがたいものになろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: しかしその温度差___、日に日に埋めがたいものになろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The 'temperature gap' was just mentioned. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: その温度差 refers back to something just introduced; は picks it up as the established topic the narrator will comment on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce it as fresh information, which is odd right after setting it up. も ('also') has nothing to add to.

contrast_examples.en: That difference (we've been discussing) is big — は.
A certain difference arose — が for first mention.

prompt.context_jp: 俊太郎の口調___静かで、それゆえに刃のように鋭かった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 俊太郎の口調___静かで、それゆえに刃のように鋭かった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for characterizing Shuntaro's tone?

feedback.correct_en: This is a descriptive characterization of his tone — は presents 俊太郎の口調 as the topic being characterized as 静か and 鋭い.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would frame it as newly identified information, awkward for an evaluative description. を is wrong grammatically.

contrast_examples.en: His voice is low — characterizing with は.
A small voice was heard — new sound, が.

prompt.context_jp: 背後で扉___控えめに開く気配があった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 背後で扉___控えめに開く気配があった。
prompt.prompt_en: A door opens behind her — unexpectedly. Which particle fits?

feedback.correct_en: A door opening behind her is a fresh, unexpected event — が marks it as new information intruding on the scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the door, (it opens)...', treating a specific door as a known topic — unnatural here. に marks direction/time, not the subject.

contrast_examples.en: A door opened — new event, が.
That door (we know) is old — topic, は.

prompt.context_jp: 寛の頬___青白く、いつもの穏やかな輪郭が微かに崩れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 寛の頬___青白く、いつもの穏やかな輪郭が微かに崩れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for describing Hiroshi's cheeks?

feedback.correct_en: Hiroshi has just entered the scene as topic; the narrator characterizes him via his cheeks with は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would push 頬 as new-information subject, but the scene isn't 'spotting cheeks' — it's describing his state. も would need a prior parallel.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の顔は青ざめていた。
contrast_examples.en: His face was pale — descriptive topic は.
His face went pale — observed change, が.

prompt.context_jp: 封を切る手___、開けたくないという気持ちを最後まで隠せずにいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 封を切る手___、開けたくないという気持ちを最後まで隠せずにいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits to characterize 'the hand opening the seal'?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes 'the hand' the topic and comments that it could not hide reluctance — は sets up that comment frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the hand freshly identified subject, breaking the reflective, descriptive tone. を doesn't fit the slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 震える手は止まらなかった。
contrast_examples.en: His trembling hand would not stop — topic/comment は.
Suddenly his hand trembled — new event が.

prompt.context_jp: 黄昏の光___細く差し込み、床に伸びる影が少しずつ揺れていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 黄昏の光___細く差し込み、床に伸びる影が少しずつ揺れていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for this descriptive scene opener?

feedback.correct_en: A scenic 'camera shot' with 差し込む uses が to present the twilight light as newly observed detail — matching the parallel 影が揺れていた clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would elevate '黄昏の光' to a topic being generalized about, inconsistent with the painterly flow. を doesn't fit (差し込む here is intransitive).

contrast_examples.en: The morning sun streamed in — が for scenic observation.
This light is special — は for characterizing.

prompt.context_jp: 恐怖と、それを超えたい願いと___、胸の中で同じ強さで鳴っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 恐怖と、それを超えたい願いと___、胸の中で同じ強さで鳴っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: What ties off this 'A and B' pair as the paired subject?

feedback.correct_en: The AとBと…が pattern identifies these two things specifically as what is resonating. が completes the exhaustive-listing frame.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn the pair into a loose topic, losing the 'these two, together' identification. を doesn't match 鳴る.

contrast_examples.jp: 愛と憎しみとが同居している。
contrast_examples.en: Love and hatred both coexist — AとBとが identification.
Love is strong — topic は.

prompt.context_jp: 山あいの療養先へと続く道___、一行はゆっくり登っていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 山あいの療養先へと続く道___、一行はゆっくり登っていった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks 'the road' as the path traversed?

feedback.correct_en: Movement verbs like 登る take を for the path/space traversed. 道を登る = 'ascend along the road.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the road a subject, which doesn't fit 登る here. に would mark endpoint, not the route itself.

contrast_examples.en: Climb up the slope — path を.
Climb to the mountaintop — goal に.

prompt.context_jp: 窓辺の小さな花瓶___、誰かが手折ったばかりの野の花が供えてあった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 窓辺の小さな花瓶___は、誰かが手折ったばかりの野の花が供えてあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the vase as the location where flowers are placed?

feedback.correct_en: With 供えてある (resultant state of 置く-type verb), に marks the location where the flowers now rest.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would mark a direct object, but the vase is the destination. で marks the setting of an action, not a resting place.

contrast_examples.en: A book is placed on the desk — に for resting place.
I study at the desk — で for action locus.

prompt.context_jp: ハナは長い時間、無言で銅鍋___向き合っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: ハナは長い時間、無言で銅鍋___向き合っていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle completes 向き合う ('face')?

feedback.correct_en: 向き合う takes に for the thing/person one faces off with. 銅鍋に向き合う = 'face the copper pot.'
feedback.incorrect_en: を doesn't collocate with 向き合う. で would mean 'at the pot' as a location, not the target of her facing.

contrast_examples.en: Face the problem — に partner.
Solve the problem — direct object を.

prompt.context_jp: 「来年ぐらいには このきれいな風景も もう見られなくなるかも だから 今 見えるものに ___ を感じてます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 今 見えるものに ___ を感じてます
prompt.prompt_en: What word does Mama say she feels in what she can still see?

feedback.correct_en: The chapter title and Mama's whole speech center on finding 幸せ (happiness) in what is visible now. 幸せを感じる is the natural collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 悲しみ or 後悔 would reverse Mama's grateful, life-affirming tone — she is explicitly refusing to dwell on loss.

contrast_examples.en: I feel happiness in each day.

contrast_examples.jp: 別れに悲しみを感じる。
contrast_examples.en: I feel sadness at the parting.

prompt.context_jp: 「___ をちゃんと伝えれば みんな 分かってくれるわよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___ をちゃんと伝えれば みんな 分かってくれるわよ」
prompt.prompt_en: What does the 招き猫 tell Hana to convey?

feedback.correct_en: 本心を伝える ('convey one's true feelings') is the fixed emotional-expression collocation. The next line even echoes 本心を伝える.
feedback.incorrect_en: 本番 means 'the real performance,' and 本当 is 'truth' but doesn't collocate as 本当を伝える in natural Japanese.

contrast_examples.en: Reveal one's true feelings.
Strong when it counts — different sense.

prompt.context_jp: 「いいなんてレベルを ___ 本当に すばらしいです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いいなんてレベルを ___ 本当に すばらしいです」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'beyond the level of just good'?

feedback.correct_en: レベルを超える ('exceed the level') is the standard collocation for 'beyond mere X.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 渡る crosses horizontally (bridges, rivers); 離れる means 'leave/separate from' — neither pairs naturally with レベル in this evaluative sense.

contrast_examples.jp: 想像を超える出来栄え。
contrast_examples.en: A result that exceeds imagination.
Cross a bridge — different metaphor.

prompt.context_jp: 「いいか お前の理想主義は いつも事を ___ にする 少しは大人になってくれ」
prompt.prompt_jp: お前の理想主義は いつも事を ___ にする
prompt.prompt_en: Shuntaro accuses his brother of 'ruining things.' Which idiom fits?

feedback.correct_en: 事を台なしにする = 'ruin everything / spoil things.' A set idiomatic phrase for criticism.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見事にする would mean 'make splendid' — the opposite of what Shuntaro means. 手頃にする ('make affordable/handy') doesn't fit scolding.

contrast_examples.jp: 一言で全てを台なしにした。
contrast_examples.en: He spoiled everything with one word.

contrast_examples.jp: 料理を見事に仕上げる。
contrast_examples.en: Finish the dish splendidly.

prompt.context_jp: 「社長が ___ 主治医のおかげで 最高の治療を 受けさせてもらってます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 社長が ___ 主治医のおかげで
prompt.prompt_en: What polite verb form does Mama use to describe the president's act of introducing the doctor?

feedback.correct_en: The subject is 社長が (an in-group higher-up acting on her behalf), so 〜してくださる (honoring the giver) fits perfectly.
feedback.incorrect_en: さしあげる humbles the giver (wrong direction when 社長 is the one giving). いただく would require 'social-president ni ... していただいた' with the speaker as grammatical subject, not 社長が.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生が教えてくださった。
contrast_examples.en: The teacher taught me (honor the giver).

contrast_examples.jp: 先生に教えていただいた。
contrast_examples.en: I had the teacher teach me (humble receive).

prompt.context_jp: 「健二先生には言ってたのよ "匿名なんて ___ は無理ですよ"って」
prompt.prompt_jp: 匿名なんて ___ は無理ですよ
prompt.prompt_en: Which adverb emphasizes 'you can't be anonymous forever'?

feedback.correct_en: ずっと expresses 'the whole time / forever,' which matches 'you can't stay anonymous forever.'
feedback.incorrect_en: さっと ('quickly, in a flash') and きっと ('surely') don't convey the long-duration meaning needed here.

contrast_examples.en: He kept silent the whole time.
He'll surely come — certainty, not duration.

prompt.context_jp: しかしその温度差は、日に日に ___ ものになろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: その温度差は、日に日に ___ ものになろうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word describes the gap as 'hard to close'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜がたい attaches to verb stems to mean 'hard to ~.' 埋めがたい = 'hard to fill/bridge,' matching the growing rift.
feedback.incorrect_en: 埋めやすい ('easy to fill') is the opposite nuance. 〜っぽい attaches to nouns/adjectives, not verb stems like this.

contrast_examples.en: A hard-to-believe story.
A gullible / easily-trusting person.

prompt.context_jp: 「 ___ でいたくないんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「 ___ でいたくないんです」
prompt.prompt_en: What state does Hiroshi say he no longer wants to be in?

feedback.correct_en: 独りでいる ('to be alone') is the fixed phrase for 'be by oneself.' Hiroshi is confessing he doesn't want to be alone anymore.
feedback.incorrect_en: 好きでいたくない would mean 'I don't want to remain in love,' which contradicts his coming to confess. 静かでいる is grammatical but off-tone for the moment.

contrast_examples.en: I'm afraid to be alone.
Please stay quiet — different nuance.

prompt.context_jp: Hana resolves to ask Kou to taste the chocolate without revealing she made it.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds more natural as narration for 'as a request, just to have him taste it, not as the maker'?

choices.text: 作った者としてではなく、ただ味を確かめてほしいだけの依頼として。
作った者としてじゃなくて、ただ味だけ確かめてほしいっていう依頼として。

feedback.correct_en: The narrative register of the chapter is literary. 〜としてではなく and 〜だけの依頼として keep a measured, written tone matching the surrounding prose.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatically fine but colloquial (〜じゃなくて, 〜っていう), which clashes with the surrounding literary narration.

contrast_examples.jp: 友人としてではなく、同僚として話す。
contrast_examples.en: Speak not as a friend but as a colleague — literary parallelism.

contrast_examples.jp: 友達じゃなくて同僚として話す。
contrast_examples.en: Same meaning, casual register.

prompt.context_jp: The 招き猫 gently urges Hana to speak her truth.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sentence sounds like natural, warm advice (as the 招き猫 would say it)?

choices.text: 本心をちゃんと伝えれば、みんな分かってくれるわよ。
本心をきちんと言ったら、みんなに理解されるわよ。

feedback.correct_en: 伝える + 分かってくれる is the natural warm pairing — the listener 'understands for you,' showing empathy. ちゃんと fits the colloquial, caring voice.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is grammatical but stiff: 理解される (passive, impersonal) sounds detached, and loses the giver-benefit nuance of 〜てくれる.

contrast_examples.jp: 正直に話せば分かってくれるよ。
contrast_examples.en: If you speak honestly, they'll understand you.

contrast_examples.jp: 説明すれば理解される。
contrast_examples.en: If you explain, you will be understood — flat, impersonal.

prompt.context_jp: Mama shares her acceptance of losing her sight.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as Mama's gentle, reflective speech?

choices.text: 今 見えるものに幸せを感じてます。
今 見えてるものを幸せに感じています。

feedback.correct_en: 〜に幸せを感じる is the idiomatic 'feel happiness in ~.' The に marks the source/locus of the feeling, which fits Mama's framing: 'in the things I can see, I feel happiness.'
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses を幸せに感じる, which shifts to 'perceive as happy' — grammatical but less natural and loses the 'find happiness in X' nuance.

contrast_examples.jp: 小さなことに幸せを感じる。
contrast_examples.en: I find happiness in small things.
I regard him as happy — different frame.

prompt.context_jp: Sōsuke reports his plans to Shuntaro in a formal business setting.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing fits a formal report from subordinate to superior?

choices.text: 世界最高のチョコレートであることを証明したいと思います。
世界最高のチョコレートだって証明したいって思ってます。

feedback.correct_en: In formal business speech to a superior, 〜であること and 〜と思います keep the required polite, written-style register.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses casual 〜だって and 〜って思ってます, which would sound inappropriate when reporting to the boss in this scene.

contrast_examples.jp: 最適であることを証明します。
contrast_examples.en: I will prove that it is optimal — formal.

contrast_examples.jp: 最適だって証明するよ。
contrast_examples.en: I'll prove it's the best — casual among friends.

prompt.context_jp: Hiroshi asks Hana to stay with him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural for his hesitant, heartfelt plea?

choices.text: 一緒にいてください。あの時みたいに。
一緒にいることをお願いします。あの時のように。

feedback.correct_en: 〜ていてください is the natural way to ask someone to remain. The casual 〜みたいに matches an emotional, personal plea.
feedback.incorrect_en: B sounds like a bureaucratic request. 〜ことをお願いします is overly formal, and 〜のように tilts toward written style — both clash with his trembling, intimate tone.

contrast_examples.en: Please stay by my side — natural emotional request.

contrast_examples.jp: ご同席をお願いします。
contrast_examples.en: I request your attendance — formal/business.
